title: Wearable robotics prototype inspired by an Iron Man suit with a HUD
objective: Come up with a wearable robotics prototype inspired by an Iron Man suit with a HUD
spoken: Here is the plan, sir. Wearable robotics prototype inspired by an Iron Man suit with a HUD: a wearable robotics project, planned as a bill of materials of 15 items in 8 groups and 7 stages. Cheapest version about $920 to $2,750; balanced about $6,450 to $19,350; premium about $36,800 to $113,000. These are CHE's estimates, not quotes. Time: about 10 to 35 weeks for the balanced version. Overall complexity is high. Not real today: Flight like Iron Man; Arc-reactor power; Bullet-proof full-body armor with full mobility. Start with stage 1: Exoskeleton frame and limb links, Battery pack and battery management, Sensors (IMU, joint encoders, force), CAD, body measurements and fit. Background read from Wikipedia: Powered exoskeleton.
feasibility: A walking, assist-only prototype is feasible for a skilled maker or small team. Strength amplification is research-grade; flight and weapons are not part of any version.
assumptions: One working prototype; production quantities change unit costs.
Prices are US dollar ranges for the 2026-10 market, not supplier quotes.
Cheapest means you do the work with off-the-shelf parts; balanced means good parts and some paid help; premium means top parts and professional work.
Timelines assume about 10 hours a week for the cheapest version, 40 for balanced and 120 for premium.
open_questions: One prototype, or a production run, and how many?
next_actions: Start with stage 1: Exoskeleton frame and limb links, Battery pack and battery management, Sensors (IMU, joint encoders, force), CAD, body measurements and fit.
Confirm the budget and quantity so CHE can narrow the ranges.
Get two or three real quotes for the largest cost items before buying.
